ui.title: DNA double helix
ui.realTitle: Open PDB 1BNA, the real crystal structure, in the molecule viewer
ui.unzipNote: Illustrative of replication: the two strands come apart so each one can be copied.
ui.tapHint: Tap a rung to see its letters. Drag to turn the helix.
ui.ruleAT: Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T). They are held by 2 hydrogen bonds.
ui.ruleGC: Guanine (G) always pairs with cytosine (C). They are held by 3 hydrogen bonds.
ui.strandRule: Strand 1 reads {a} here, running 5' to 3' up the helix. Strand 2 reads {b}, running the other way.
ui.closePair: {a} {an} on chain A with {b} {bn} on chain B
ui.closeBonds: {n} hydrogen bonds measured in the crystal: {d} angstroms between the facing nitrogen and oxygen atoms
ui.closeFail: The atom file could not be loaded.
ui.keys: 1 orbit, 2 fly along, 3 close-up. Arrow keys turn the view (in fly along, up and down move along the helix). Plus and minus zoom. [ and ] step through base pairs. U unzips, Space pauses, Escape goes back to orbit.
ui.alt: An illustrative 3D model of a DNA double helix, 72 base pairs and about 24 nm long, about 2 nm wide, slowly turning and drifting on a dark background. Two glowing backbones, strand 1 in blue and strand 2 in violet, wind around each other in a right-handed spiral, about 10.5 base pairs per turn, leaving a wide major groove and a narrow minor groove. Flat coloured rungs join the strands: A-T pairs in orange and yellow, joined by 2 faint hydrogen bond links, and G-C pairs in green and mint, joined by 3. Labels at the ends mark 5' and 3', showing that the strands run in opposite directions. Fly along moves the camera down the length of the helix. Close-up shows the real atoms of one base pair from the crystal structure PDB 1BNA as balls and sticks, with the measured hydrogen bonds as dotted lines.
ui.nogl: The 3D view needs WebGL, which is off or missing in this browser. Here is a flat drawing and a text description instead.
ui.noglFig: Flat drawing of a DNA double helix with coloured base pair rungs

facts.t: DNA is two strands twisted around each other into a right-handed double helix.
The strands are antiparallel: the 3' end of one faces the 5' end of the other.
The helix is about 2 nm wide, the same all along its length.
Each base pair sits 0.34 nm from the next.
Textbooks round to 10 base pairs and 3.4 nm per turn. Measured in solution, DNA turns once every 10.4 base pairs, plus or minus 0.1, so this model uses 10.5, which makes one turn about 3.6 nm long.
A pairs with T through 2 hydrogen bonds; G pairs with C through 3.
The twist leaves evenly spaced major and minor grooves along the helix.
The close-up atoms are real coordinates from PDB 1BNA, a 12 base pair crystal with the sequence CGCGAATTCGCG. This model repeats that sequence six times.
